summary: Heinrich Kiepert worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1828–1836) and Frederick William University Berlin (1837). He held posts at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir zu Weimar (1845–1852) and Frederick William University Berlin (1859).

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer worked in linguistics and other fields, studying at Leipzig University (~1819–1824). He founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft and held a post at Leipzig University from ~1835 to 1888.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn (~1890–1894). He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, Humboldt University of Berlin (1909), and the Prussian Academy of Sciences (~1912–1943).
Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Bernhard Hirzel (~1836–1838) and held a post at the University of Zurich from ~1841 to 1889.

Heinrich Stönner was an Indologist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1896–1901). From 1901 to 1931, he held posts at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, including Hilfsarbeiter, Direktorial-Assistent, Kustos, and Abteilungsleiter.
Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1863–1867). He served as a professor at the Kreuzschule from ~1872 to 1907.

Heinrich Wenzel worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, and Leipzig, working under Léon Feer, Friedrich Max Müller, Heinrich August Jäschke, and Georg von der Gabelentz. He completed his habilitation at Leipzig University in 1886.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under Rudolf von Roth, Albrecht Weber, Wilhelm Scherer, Siegfried Goldschmidt, and Ernst Windisch. His posts included Greifswald (~1881–1901), Berlin (~1901–1910), Heidelberg (1923–1938), and Columbia University.

Heinz Bechert was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1954–1956). He held posts at Saarland University (~1957–1964), the University of Göttingen (1974), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1973–2005).

Heinz Mode worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under George Peiris Malalasekera, Otto Fischer, and at the University of Basel (~1937–1942). He became Professor of Oriental Archaeology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1948.
Helen Hardacre is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She held a post in the Department of Religion at Princeton University (~1980–1989) and joined Harvard University around 1989.

Helen J. Baroni specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt (~1988–1993). In ~1993, she took up a post at the University of Hawaii.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979 to 1984. She held an academic post at Rice University beginning around 1990.

Helga Uebach was a Tibetologist who earned her Ph.D. at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1961–1967). In 1964, she held a post as wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Hellmut Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1928–1932). From ~1948 to 1973, he served as Professor of Chinese Studies and Associate Director of the Far Eastern Institute at the University of Washington.
Helmer Smith was an Indologist and linguist specializing in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Lund University (~1927–1936) and Uppsala University (~1936–1947).
Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Frank-Richard Hamm (~1965–1973) and held a post at the University of Bonn from ~1974 to 2001.

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Freiburg and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Giuseppe Tucci, and Ferdinand Diederich Lessing. His posts included the Prussian Academy, Ahnenerbe, Hamburg, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1989–2014), the University of Vienna (~1990–2014), and served as director of the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2007–2014).
